{{Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics}}
The '''women's pursuit''' competition of the [[Biathlon at the 2026 Winter Olympics|2026 Winter Olympics]] was held on 15 February,<!-- 2026--> at the [[South Tyrol Arena|Anterselva Biathlon Arena]] in [[Rasen-Antholz]].<ref name="schedule">{{cite web|url=https://www.biathlonworld.com/calendar?SeasonId=2526&CupLevel=1&EventId=BT2526SWRLOG__|title=2026 Olympic Games – Antholz-Anterselva|publisher=[[International Biathlon Union|IBU]]|access-date=15 February 2026}}</ref> [[Lisa Vittozzi]] of Italy won the event, [[Maren Kirkeeide]] of Norway, the winner of sprint who started first, won the silver medal, and [[Suvi Minkkinen]] of Finland won bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/lisa-vittozzi-brings-home-glorious-gold-italy-womens-10km-pursuit|title=Lisa Vittozzi brings home glorious biathlon gold for Italy in women’s 10km pursuit|publisher=NBC Olympics|accessdate=27 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/olympics-biathlon-womens-pursuit-b43f748240bb27da53658f5357315c9b|title=Lisa Vittozzi secures Italy’s first Olympic gold medal in biathlon with pursuit win|publisher=APNews|accessdate=27 February 2026}}</ref> Vittozzi's medal was the first gold medal of Italy in biathlon, and Minkkinen won her first Olympic medal.

==Background==
The pursuit is contingent on the results of the sprint held on the previous day. [[Maren Kirkeeide]], the winner of the sprint, will start first, followed by the silver medalist [[Océane Michelon]] in 4 seconds and the bronze medalist [[Lou Jeanmonnot]] in 24 seconds. The 2022 champion, [[Marte Olsbu Røiseland]], and the bronze medalist, [[Tiril Eckhoff]], retired from competitions. The 2022 silver medalist, [[Elvira Öberg]], finished the 27th in sprint and will start 1:38 behind Kirkeeide. Prior to the Olympics, Jeanmonnot was leading the total standings of the [[2025–26 Biathlon World Cup]], and [[Suvi Minkkinen]] was leading the pursuit standings. Minkkinen will start 50 seconds behind Kirkeeide. The [[Biathlon World Championships 2025 – Women's pursuit|2025 World champion]] was [[Franziska Preuß]], who will start one minute behind Kirkeeide.
